engine.installed_with: npm install chepta@0.6.1 in a separate folder; Lab's package.json and package-lock.json not changed

interface: command line: chepta request <file>; exit codes 0 ok, 2 invalid_input, 3 missing_data, 4 unsupported, 5 not_converged, 6 cancelled, 7 out_of_time, 8 error, 1 the command line itself

source.paper: Piotrowski & Kubica 2021, Processes 9, 1425, doi 10.3390/pr9081425, CC BY 4.0

settings.value: UNIQUAC liquid, ideal-gas vapour; CHEPTA applies its chemical theory (dimers) to acetic acid in the vapour; CHEPTA's default UNIQUAC pair sets
settings.locator: Section 2.1, p.5 (UNIQUAC for VLE and LLE)
settings.reason: The paper names UNIQUAC but prints neither its parameters (Chemcad 7's) nor the vapour model. CHEPTA's own UNIQUAC sets are reused (AGENTS.md).

settings.value: 100 kPa everywhere, no pressure drop
settings.locator: Table A2, column 'Pres. Bar' = 1 for every stream, pp.13-14
settings.reason: Section 2 (p.4) says 'atmospheric pressure' (101.325 kPa, 1.3 % higher); the printed 1 bar is used.

settings.value: Table A2 mass flows and compositions; 17 is at 20 C
settings.locator: Table A2 streams 1, 2, 17, pp.13-14

settings.value: 18.0 C instead of the printed 15 C
settings.locator: Table A2 streams 1-3 (15 C); CHEPTA runs u-htxr2-15C and secA-feeds-15C-17C (refused)
settings.reason: Pure acetic acid at 15 C is below its triple point (289.81 K = 16.66 C in CHEPTA's ChemSep-based record), and CHEPTA refuses a liquid with acetic acid below that temperature even mixed with ethanol (OUT_OF_RANGE). The two feeds cool by about 1 K on mixing, so 18 C, the lowest whole degree for which CHEPTA's MIX 1 outlet (about 17.0 C) stays above it, is used for both (17 C was refused, run secA-feeds-17C). Effect: HTXR 2 heats from about 17 C instead of 15 C.

settings.locator: Table A2 stream 4

settings.value: ethanol + acetic acid -> ethyl acetate + water (liquid), acetic acid conversion per pass 0.7703
settings.locator: Table A2 streams 5 and 6
settings.reason: 1 - (53292 x 4.74 %)/(53292 x 20.64 %) = 0.7703. The paper's kinetics (Eqs. 1-3, pp.5-6, after Atalay) cannot be used: the catalyst concentration and the units of C are not given; CHEPTA has no reactor-evaporator (a boiling, reacting liquid whose only outlet is its vapour). The reactor's conversion is therefore IMPOSED from the paper, not predicted; its outlet temperature and duty are results.

settings.value: saturated vapour (VF = 1) at 100 kPa
settings.locator: Section 2, p.4 ('The vapors from the reactor (Stream 6)'); Table A2 streams 5 and 6 both 53,292 kg/h
settings.reason: Everything that enters leaves as vapour; the printed 90 C is compared, not imposed.

settings.value: absorber-type column, no condenser or reboiler, 8 equilibrium stages, reflux 27 on stage 1, reactor vapour 6 on stage 8, adiabatic
settings.locator: Table 1 p.11 (8 stages, feed stage 8, R/V 0.61); Section 3.2 p.6 ('reactor vapors are fed to the last stage ... reflux (Stream 27) ... onto the first stage'); Figure 1 p.4 (no condenser or reboiler drawn)
settings.reason: Stage efficiency not given: equilibrium stages assumed. R/V = 0.61 is not a setting here: it equals stream 27 over stream 8 on mass (60000/98380 = 0.610, derived). Section 3.2 asks for at least 14 stages; Table 1 says 8 (paper's discrepancy kept).

settings.value: saturated liquid (VF = 0) at 100 kPa
settings.locator: Table A2 streams 8, 9 (both printed 70 C); CHEPTA run u-htxr6-70C
settings.reason: At the printed 70 C and 100 kPa CHEPTA finds stream 8's composition 72 % vapour (just above its bubble point); the stream goes to an extractor, so total condensation is taken. Its temperature is compared with 70 C.

settings.what: cut between sections A and B
settings.value: acetic acid removed from stream 9 and not a component of section B
settings.locator: Table A2: acetic acid 0.01 mass % in streams 9-13, 16, 18-20, 22-28, 0.00 % in 14, 15, 21; CHEPTA runs u-htxr10, u-htxr12, u-htxr18, u-htxr19, u-scds11-* (refused)
settings.reason: With acetic acid present CHEPTA refuses every stream that holds two liquids (the three-phase flash with the acid chemical theory is not built). The acid dropped is reported in every run; it is not replaced by a split.

settings.value: a mixer whose outlet is brought to saturated liquid (VF = 0): CHEPTA's heater block with two inlets; its duty is reported
settings.locator: Figure 1 p.4 (MIX 7, no duty); Table A2 stream 10 (70 C, the extractor's feed); CHEPTA run secB-mix7-adiabatic (refused)
settings.reason: Adiabatic mixing of the saturated azeotrope 9 and the product column distillate 15 leaves a few % vapour in CHEPTA, and CHEPTA's Extraction block refuses a feed with any vapour (BAD_INPUT), although its stages are at 27 C. The small condensing duty this adds is not in the paper and is reported.

settings.value: countercurrent equilibrium stages, isothermal at 27 C; organic 10 the feed, water 19 the solvent
settings.locator: Table 1 p.11 (70 C, W/A = 1); Table A2 streams 11 (27 C) and 20 (41 C); CHEPTA run u-extr8-*-70C (refused)
settings.reason: Table 1's 70 C is not usable as the stage temperature: the paper's feed at 70 C and 100 kPa is 77 % vapour in CHEPTA (refused, run u3-extr8-1stage-70C-feed70C), and with a saturated-liquid feed the 70 C extractor runs (u3-extr8-1stage-70C) but its outlets are partly vapour (raffinate VF 0.05), which CHEPTA returns as ok without a warning. The paper's own outlets (27 C organic, 41 C aqueous) imply an adiabatic extractor, which CHEPTA's isothermal block cannot do; 27 C, where the raffinate leaves, is taken, with a 41 C variant. W/A = 1 is not a setting: stream 19 / stream 10 = 113276/113256 = 1.000 (derived)

settings.value: not given in the paper; 1 to 8 stages run, plant run with the number stated in the run manifest
settings.reason: The paper gives no stage count, efficiency or contactor type for EXTR 8.

settings.value: fraction to stream 26 = 60000/87314 = 0.68718
settings.locator: Table A2 streams 11, 26
settings.reason: The round 60,000 kg/h suggests a flow specification in Chemcad; CHEPTA's splitter takes fractions only.

settings.locator: Table A2 stream 27
Table A2 stream 13

settings.value: 35 stages (1 the condenser, 35 the reboiler), feed stage 15, total condenser, R/D = 3, bottoms 141.5 kmol/h (Table A2 stream 16); two liquids allowed on the stages (VLL)
settings.locator: Table 1 p.11 (35 stages, feed 15, R/D 3); Section 3.4 p.8 ('purity greater than 99.9 %', 'EA content in the product (99.9 wt%)'); Table A2 stream 16
settings.reason: Chemcad's stage count assumed to include condenser and reboiler, as CHEPTA's does. Total condenser assumed (stream 14 all recycled). Section 3.4 places the best feed between stages 4 and 6, Table 1 says 15 (paper's discrepancy kept). The product purity is then a result, compared with 99.90 mass %. Variant (unit run u3-scds11-purity): the purity 99.90 mass % (Section 3.4) in place of the bottoms flow.

settings.value: duty 0 kW
settings.locator: Table 1 p.11 (S2: 0)

settings.value: pump to 100 kPa (no pressure rise)
settings.locator: Figure 1 p.4 (grey round symbol between MIX 13 and EXTR 8); streams 18 and 19 identical in Table A2
settings.reason: The paper does not name block 14; its symbol looks like Chemcad's pump. It changes nothing in Table A2.

settings.locator: Table A2 stream 28

settings.value: 18 stages, feed stage 9, total condenser, R/D = 2, distillate 394.6 kmol/h
settings.locator: Table 1 p.11 (18 stages, feed 9, R/D 2); Table A2 stream 21
settings.reason: The paper does not say which second specification Chemcad used; stream 21's molar flow is taken. Section 3.5 (p.10) asks < 0.01 wt% organics in the bottoms, but stream 22 prints 0.03 wt% (paper's discrepancy kept).

settings.value: fraction to wastewater 25 = 20000/115797 = 0.17272
settings.locator: Table A2 streams 22, 25
settings.reason: A fixed wastewater flow with a fixed fresh water feed has no steady state unless they match exactly; with a fraction the water loop settles. Stream 25's flow is compared with 20,000 kg/h.

settings.locator: Table A2 stream 24

settings.what: streams 8 (VF = 1), 9, 10, 14, 15, 21, 23 (VF = 0) as feeds of unit runs
settings.value: saturated (VF given) where the printed temperature lies at or above CHEPTA's bubble point; stream 3 at 18 C (see feeds 1 and 2)
settings.reason: Condensates printed at 70-71 C; see HTXR 6.

settings.what: tear streams and the coupling across the cut
settings.value: starting guesses from Table A2; successive substitution of streams 9, 21, 27 by Lab's script
settings.reason: Starting points only; a converged answer does not depend on them.

Last residuals: material 31.96 mol/s, equilibrium 0.0712, energy 1603000 W, specifications 0. This does not show that the column has no solution: try other feeds (more liquid or less gas), more stages, other feed stages, or stage duties that remove the heat of absorption.. What usually helps: a purge or a smaller recycle fraction (a recycle with no way out keeps growing), a guess for the tear stream (S7) close to the answer, another tear stream, another convergence method, or more iterations.
